description_en: Bhīmasena Mandira is located at Bhindyaḥtvāḥ, Kathmandu. It faces east and has three roofs. Usually, the sanctum (garbhagṛha) of a temple is built on the ground floor. However, this is not the case in the Bhīmasena Mandira. Its sanctum is on the first floor where a Bhīmasena statue is consecrated as the main deity. Two divine (Arjuna and Draupadī) and two human (Dhusi Āḥju and Dhusi Ajimā) statues are also installed inside the sanctum. According to theDevamālā Vaṃśāvalī(2013, 43), there is no Arjuna statue in the temple. It mentions that both statues are of Bhīmasena, one in vigorous form (krodhamudrā), and another in peaceful form (śāntamudrā). The ground floor of the temple is occupied by three shops. Local residents believe that the abovementioned human statues help to neutralize back pain. Therefore, male and female devotees who are having back pain respectively worship Dhusi Āḥju and Dhusi Ājimā. All of these five statues are made of mud.The Bhīmasena Temple was constructed by a local ruler (mahāpātra) of Kathmandu. In the medieval period, when Bhaktapur was the capital of the Kathmandu Valley, twelvemahāpātraswere given the responsibility of ruling twelve different administrative territories. Eight out of these twelve territories were considered strategically important. Themahāpātraswere called Thakūjuju (Ṭhakurī kings) in Newari. In 1484 CE, the eleventh of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha in NS 604, Ratna Malla, Yakṣa Malla’s son, captured Kathmandu by assassinating all eightmahāpātras(cf.Śreṣṭha2059, 14-17). The group of thesemahāpātrasremained influential in the society even after they lost their administrative power. Toyūju Thakura, a descendant of one of thosemahāpātraswho used to rule the territory of the lower Kvāḥ Bāhāḥ, constructed the Bhīmasena Temple, consecrated a Bhīmasena statue inside its sanctum, and established aguṭhīin 1564 CE the third of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha in NS 660 (cf.Śreṣṭha2059, 40). A copperplate inscription detailing this event has been already published.Note that the chronicles record a different date regarding the construction of the temple. For example theDevamālā Vaṃśāvalī(2013, 43) andBhāṣā Vamśāvalī(part 2, 2023, 28-2) mention that Toyūkhvāḥ, a Ṭhakurī ruler, constructed the Bhīmasena Mandira and consecrated a Bhīmasena statue inside its sanctum in 1140 CE (NS 260). TheNepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī(17.4-6) too mentions this event but does not record its date. However, the abovementioned copperplate inscription, detailing the construction of this temple, nullifies the information recorded in these chronicles.There is a popular legendary story in the Newari society regarding this Bhīmasena. It mentions that the aforementioned Mahāpātra Tuyūkhvāḥ Malla married Padmāvatī, a daughter of Abhayadeva, a powerful Sāmanta of Dolakhā. Her parental family sent a Jyāpu caste member to Kathmandu with her, making him carry the dowry. Tuyūkhvāḥ Malla (Thaku Juju) gave this Jyāpu the responsibility to cultivate the former’s field at Chhauni, Kathmandu. However, he did not cultivate the field even until after the monsoon started in Āṣāḍha. Thus, Tuyūkhvāḥ became angry with that Jyāpu. Having seen the disappointed Tuyūkhvāḥ, the Jyāpu asked him to close his eyes for a moment. As soon as Tuyūkhvāḥ opened his eyes, the Jyāpu had already planted rice in the field. Tuyūkhvāḥ then realized that the Jyāpu was not an ordinary farmer. He apologized for his behaviour and asked for his real identity. The Jyāpu was, in fact, Bhīmasena. He manifested his real form and told Tuyūkhvāḥ that he is not only Bhīmasena, but also an incarnation of Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara (Buṅgadyaḥ) and came to Kathmandu for the benefit of Newar traders of the valley. For this reason, Tuyūkhvāḥ constructed this temple for him and consecrated his statue.It is believed that this Bhīmasena travels around the city every evening and wherever his eyes rest, that shop receives a lot of customers. Therefore, businessmen worship him as Bhiṃmhaḥ Dyaḥ, auspicious deity (based on a personal communication with a Dyaḥpāḥlāḥ of the Temple from a Ḍaṅgola caste, female, age 68). In 1655 CE (NS 775) King Pratāpa Malla had installed the abovementioned Draupadī statue in the sanctum.The temple was renovated in 1959 CE (VS 2016) with the active participation of the local community and was stewarded by King Mahendra.The descendants of the Thaku Jujus (Ṭhakurī kings) perform the daily worship in the temple. Two Ḍaṅgola families have been taking care of the temple. A special worship to Bhīmasena takes place on the eleventh of the bright fortnight of Māgha (Bhīmasena Ekādaśī). Once in every twelve years, the Bhīmasena statue is carried to thephalcāwhich is located around forty meters from the temple. It is believed that thephalcāis his real home.
description_ne: काठमाडौंको भीमसेनस्थानाम तीन तह छाना राखी पूर्वाभिमुख गरी बनाइएको भीमसेनको मन्दिर रहेको छ । भीमसेनको मन्दिर रहेकोले टोलको नाम भीमसेनस्थान रहेको हो । सामान्यतया मन्दिरको भुइँ तलामा मुख्य देवता राखिने भएपनि यस मन्दिरको भुइँ तलामा तीनवटा पसल राखिएका छन् । मन्दिरको पहिलो तलामा गर्भगृह बनाई भीमसेन सहित अन्य चार गरी जम्मा पाँचवटा मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएका छन् ।[1]गर्भगृहभित्र दक्षिणतिर भीमसेन, उत्तरतिर अर्जुनको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ भने भीमसेन र अर्जुन[2]को बीचमा द्रौपदीको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ ।यी देवताहरू बाहेक गर्भगृहभित्रभित्र अन्य दुईवटा मूर्ति पनि स्थापना गरिएका छन् । गर्भगृहको दक्षिणमा धुसि आ:जु र धुसि अजिमा भनी दुईवटा मानव मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएका छन् । यी दुबै मानव मूर्तिलाई ढाड दुखेको निको पार्ने देवताको रूपमा पूजा गरिन्छ । पुरुषको ढाड दुखेमा धुसि आ:जु र महिलाको ढाड दुखेमा धुसि अजिमा पूजा गरेमा निको हुने विश्वास गरिन्छ । यी पाँचै मूर्तिहरू माटोले बनाइएका हुन् ।यो मन्दिरको निर्माण काठमाडौंका महापात्रहरूले गरेका थिए । पूर्वमध्यकालमा नेपालको राजधानी भक्तपुर हुँदा काठमाडौंमा १२ जना महापात्रहरूलाई १२ ठाउँको प्रशासन चलाउने जिम्मेवारी दिइएको थियो । ती १२ मध्ये ८ ठाउँलाई प्रमुख ठाउँ मानिन्थ्यो । ती महापात्रहरूलाई नेवारीमाथकूजुजु(ठकुरी राजा) भनिन्थ्यो । नेसं ६०४ वैशाख शुक्ल ११ (सन् १४८४) मा राजा यक्ष मल्लका माहिला छोरा रत्न मल्लले आठैजना महापात्रहरूलाई मारेर काठमाडौंमा कब्जा गरेका थिए (Śreṣṭha2059, 14-17) । सत्ताबाट बाहिरिए पनि समाजमा ती महापात्रहरूको प्रभाव कायमै थियो ।ती महापात्रहरूमध्ये तल्लो क्वा: बाहा:मा शासन चलाउने महापात्रका सन्तान तोयूजु थकुरले नेसं ६६० वैशाख शुक्ल ३ (सन् १५६४) मा भीमसेन स्थापना गरी जग्गा गुठी राखिदिएका थिए (Śreṣṭha2059, 40) । यस सम्बन्धी ताम्रपत्र नै प्रकाशमा आइसकेको छ । पछिल्लो कालमा लेखिएका वंशावलीहरूमा  नेसं २६० मा तोयूख्वा नाम गरेका ठकुरी राजाले नेसं २६० मा मन्दिर सहित ठूलो मूर्ति बनाई भीमसेन स्थापना गरे भनी लेखिएको छ (देवमाला वंशावली2013, 43 रभाषा वंशावली, part 2, 2023, 28-29) ।नेपालीकभूपवंशावली(17.4-6) मा पनि यही कुरा लेखिएको छ तर मिति दिइएको छैन । भीमसेन स्थापना सम्बन्धी ताम्रपत्र नै प्राप्त भइसकेकोले वंशावलीमा लेखिएको कुरालाई प्रामाणिक मान्न सकिन्न । यस भीमसेनबारे नेवार समाजमा एउटा किम्बदन्ती प्रचलित छ । किम्बदन्ती अनुसार काठमाडौंका तुयुख्वा: मल्ल (ताम्रपत्रमा तोयूजु थकुर) नामका ठकुरी राजा (महापात्र) को दोलखाका शक्तिशाली सामन्त अभयदेवकी छोरी पद्मावतीसँग विवाह भएको थियो । बेहुली पद्मावतीको दाइजो बोकाएर एकजना ज्यापुलाई पनि काठमाडौंमा पठाइएको थियो ।थकूजुजुले छाउनीमा रहेको खेतको हेरविचार गर्ने जिम्मा ती ज्यापुलाई दिए । असार महिनासम्म पनि ती ज्यापुले खेतमा केही रोपेका थिएनन् । आफ्नो खेत बाँझै रहेको देखेर थकूजुजुले ज्यापुलाई गाली गर्न थाले । ज्यापुले एकछिन आँखा बन्द गर्नुहोस् भनेपछि थकूजुजुले आफ्नो आँखा बन्द गरे । आँखा खोलेर हेर्दा सम्पूर्ण खेतमा धान रोपिसकेको पाए । ती ज्यापु साधारण मान्छे होइनन् भन्ने थाहा पाएपछि थकूजुजुले माफी मागी उनको परिचय मागे ।ज्यापुले एक हातमा कमलको फूल, अर्को हातमा सुनको गदा धारण गरेका, गलामा सर्पको माला लगाएका, विभिन्न रत्न जडित सुनको मुकुट धारण गरेका रक्त वर्णको भीमसेनको रूपमा दर्शन दिए । भीमसेनले आफू पद्मपाणि लोकेश्वर (बुंगद्य:) को अवतार भएको र नेपाल मण्डलका व्यापारीहरूको उत्थान गर्नको लागि आएको बताए । भीमसेनले इच्छानुसार थकूजुजुले मन्दिर बनाई भीमसेन स्थापना गरिदिए ।हरेक दिन साँझपख भीमसेन डुल्न जाँदा जुन-जुन पसलमा उनको नजर पर्थ्यो ती पसलहरूमा ग्राहकहरूको घुइँचो लाग्थ्यो । सबै व्यापारीहरूले उनलाईभिंम्ह द्य:अर्थात् असल देवताको रूपमा पुज्न थाले (Dyaḥpāḥlāḥ of the temple from a Dangol caste, female, age 68) । नेसं ७७५ (सन् १६५५) मा राजा प्रताप मल्लले द्रौपदीको मूर्ति स्थापना गरेका थिए । बेला-बेलामा यो मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार कार्य हुँदै आइरहेको छ । विसं २०१६ सालमा पन्नामानसिंह मल्ल वडाका अध्यक्ष रहँदा स्थानीय बासिन्दाहरूको सकृयतामा राजा महेन्द्र वीरविक्रम शाहदेवले मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गराएका थिए ।यो मन्दिर थकूजुजु (ठकुरी राजा) हरुले निर्माण गरेको हुनाले प्रत्येक दिन उनीहरूले नै नित्यपूजा गरी बेलुकी आरती दिने गरिन्छ । यस मन्दिरमा लाखे ननिमा बस्ने डंगोल थरका दुई परिवारलाई द्य:पा:ला:को रूपमा नियुक्त गरिएको छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष माघ शुक्ल एकादशी (भीम एकादशी) मा भीमसेन उपवास बस्ने दिन हुनाले विशेष पूजा गरिन्छ । प्रत्येक १२ वर्षमा एकपल्ट भीमसेनलाई उनको आफ्नो घरमा लग्ने भनेर मन्दिरभन्दा करीब ४० मिटर दक्षिणमा रहेको फल्चामा राख्ने गरिन्छ ।Footnotes^मन्दिरको पहिलो तलामा फोटो खिच्न मनाही गरिएको छ र गर्भगृहको नाप नाप लिने अनुमित पनि दिइएको छैन ।^सर्वसाधारणले यसलाई अर्जुन मानेपनि वंशावलीमा यसलाई भीमसेन नै भनिएको छ  । वंशावलीमा क्रोध र शान्त मुद्रा गरी भीमसेनका दुईवटा मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको कुरा लेखिएको छ (देवमालावंशावली2013, 43) ।

historical_events.event_name: Installation of the Statue of Bhīmasena
historical_events.event_description: Toyūju Thaku, amahāpātraof the lower Kvāḥ Bāhāḥ, installed the Bhīmasena Statue, formed aguṭhī,and made a land endowment.

This event is not related to the Bhīmasena Temple. On the bottom part of the copperplate inscription, which records the consecration of the Bhīmasena Statue, it is mentioned that King Mahendra Malla constructed theTao Devala(the Taleju Mandira) in 1564 CE (NS 660).The copperplate inscription only mentions NS 684 Mārgaśīrṣa. The date mentioned on a record that details themandira’s construction, also mentions tenth day of the dark fortnight in Mārgaśīrṣa on NS 684 (Vajrācārya G.2033, 116).

historical_events.event_name: Installation a Stone Inscription, Praising Bhīmasena, and Establishment of a Statue of Draupadī
historical_events.event_description: King Pratāpa Malla established this stone inscription praising Bhīmasena. It also records the installation of the Draupadī Statue in the sanctum.
A Mānandharaguṭhī, comprising of thirty-seven members and headed by Mānandhara Jesta Taosi, offered thistoraṇato Bhīmasena.
Mānadhra Jayadeo (Mānandhara Jayadeva) offered it to Bhīmasena.
Rañjikā (Rañjitakāra) Jayadharmma from Cikãmugala Ṭola offered it to Bhīmasena.

The temple was renovated during the reign of King Mahendra, when Pannā Māna Siṃha Malla, one of the descandants of Toyūju Thaku, was the Ward Chairperson. The local community also actively participated in the renovation process.

historical_events.event_name: Replacing Jhĩgaṭī Roof with Copper Sheets
historical_events.event_description: The upper two roofs of the temple were already cladded in gold-plated brass. Thejhĩgaṭītiles of the first roof were also replaced with copper sheets. This work was supported by the office of the Ward Number 20, the Department of Archaeology, and local patrons.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of a Lion Pillar and Offering a Patāḥ
historical_events.event_description: During the reign of King Rājendra Vikrama Śāha, Tulādhara Rāvata and Mānandhara Jaganārāyaṇa (Jagannārāyaṇa), residents of Maru Ṭola, offered the lion pillar including a gold-plated lion statue resting atop of it. They also offered thepatāḥto the deity.
Dhanalakṣmī, her son Saṅkhanārā̃, and other family members jointly repaired the Jalaharyoparijinālaṅkṛta Caitya (KAT0920-005) during the reing of King Surendra Śāha (r. 1847-1881).
Since the inscription is heavily damaged, its content remains obscure.
